about: Hard replay tasks: real orchd tasks that failed review several times before landing. Each starts at the parent of its landed commit; `check` runs that commit's own integration tests (behaviour over RPC, exact names, counted). Requests name the graded interface.

tasks.name: worktrees-cleanup
tasks.request:
orchd worktrees live inside the repo under .sushiai/worktrees and are removed when a task no longer needs them

orchd never removes a task's worktree (not on done, archive or delete); 48 sibling worktrees took 43 GB, almost all build output. Repo-agnostic changes:
1. Location: new task worktrees are created at `<repo>/.sushiai/worktrees/<slug>` (setting `worktreeRoot`, default that path; a relative value is resolved against the repo root). orchd adds `/.sushiai/` to the repo's `.git/info/exclude` (never edits tracked files). Existing tasks keep their recorded worktree path.
2. Cleanup: when a task ends `done` (its work committed on its branch, or landed on its parent), orchd removes its worktree (`git worktree remove --force` is fine then: the commit exists) and records `worktreeRemoved: true` plus a decision line. A parent removes its own worktree when it finishes. `task.archive` of a stopped/failed task first saves any uncommitted work (tracked + untracked, not ignored) to the task's existing wip ref (git::wip_ref), then removes the worktree. `task.delete` removes worktree and branch. A task that is running, waiting, queued or drafting never loses its worktree.
3. Restore: `task.start`/retry/unarchive of a task whose worktree is gone recreates it from its branch (and restores the wip ref's changes if any) before the next attempt.
4. `orchd gc --data <dir> --socket <sock> [--dry-run]` and RPC `worktrees.gc`: applies rule 2 to every existing task of every repo (done -> remove; archived stopped/failed -> save wip then remove; a worktree with no task record at all is only listed, never removed), then `git worktree prune`; reports each path, the action and the bytes freed. Dry run changes nothing.
5. This repo only: add `.sushiai/` to .gitignore and to the ignore lists that prettier/eslint/node --test globs use here, so the main checkout's CI never walks nested worktrees; prove `npm run ci` ignores a dummy file under .sushiai/worktrees.
Release fragment docs/releases/unreleased/orchestrator-worktree-cleanup.md.

The graded interface: task fields `worktree`, `branch`, `worktreeRemoved`; RPCs task.archive/unarchive/start/delete and `worktrees.gc {dryRun}` returning `worktrees: [{path, action}]` and `freedBytes`.
tasks.check: git show 13cfbfa:orchd/tests/worktrees.rs > orchd/tests/zz_ref_check.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet --test zz_ref_check -- --exact new_worktree_lives_under_sushiai_and_done_removes_it_but_keeps_the_commit archiving_a_stopped_task_saves_its_edits_and_unarchive_restores_them starting_a_task_whose_worktree_is_gone_recreates_it delete_removes_the_worktree_and_the_branch gc_removes_done_and_archived_worktrees_but_never_running_or_unknown_ones 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 5 passed'

tasks.name: run-fingerprint
tasks.request:
orchd run fingerprint: record the real model, harness version and prompt inputs per run

orchd stores only the model alias it asked for (`model: "sonnet"`); when Claude Code started resolving `sonnet` to claude-sonnet-5-5, A/B pairs silently mixed two models. Record what actually ran, repo-agnostically, for every run (plan, implement, review, advisor, audit):
- Claude: the init event's `model` and `claude_code_version`, and the result event's `modelUsage` keys (all real model ids used, incl. subagents). Codex: the model it reports and `codex --version` (cached per daemon start). Store on the attempt as `fingerprint: {models: [..], harness, harnessVersion, promptHash}` where promptHash is a short hash of the inputs orchd controls (the brief template version constant, the argv minus paths/ids, the run settings JSON minus secrets). Do not hash the task-specific brief text.
- `orchd ab` and `orchd eval` group rows by (variant, fingerprint-without-promptHash models+harnessVersion) and print the fingerprint in the row; a report mixing fingerprints for one variant says so on a line.
- Old attempts without a fingerprint load and show `-`.
Mirror the field in src/orchestrator/types.ts; show `model (harness version)` in the panel's attempt line instead of the alias when present. Release fragment line in docs/releases/unreleased/orchestrator-ab-variants.md.

The graded interface: each attempt in task.get has `fingerprint: {models: [..], harness, harnessVersion, promptHash}`.
tasks.check: git show ae416d0:orchd/tests/task_loop.rs > orchd/tests/zz_ref_check.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet --test zz_ref_check -- --exact an_attempt_stores_the_model_and_harness_version_the_run_reported 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 1 passed'

tasks.name: eval-graded-checks
tasks.request:
orchd eval: pass^k, cost per successful task, graded checks, and a harvested candidate set

Make `orchd eval`/`orchd ab --eval` measure what labs report (tau-bench pass^k, SWE-bench graded checks), repo-agnostically:
1. Eval set entries may carry `check` (a shell command, run from the repo root) that grades the result: after an eval task ends `done`, orchd runs the check against the task's final commit in a throwaway worktree (never the task's own) with the verify timeout and records `evalCheck: {code, tail}` on the task. A task counts as a success only when it is done and its check (if any) exits 0. Add `check` to the four tasks in orchd/evals/set-1.json where the reference commit's own tests prove it (read each reference commit; use exact test names so zero matches cannot pass).
2. `orchd ab --eval` headline per variant: success rate (pass@1 over all runs), pass^k (share of eval tasks where all k repeats of that variant succeeded; k = the repeat count seen), cost per successful task (total $ / successes), median minutes to done; rows grouped by variant and run fingerprint (stage 2) as `orchd ab` already does. A paired table: per task, each variant's successes/k and $.
3. `orchd eval harvest --data <dir> --repo <path> --out <file>` writes candidate entries from real finished tasks of that repo that are not eval tasks: {name (slug of title), base (the task's baseSha), request (the original request, else goal), reference (the landed commit if done, else null), source: task id, outcome: done|failed|stopped}. It never edits a set; a person or the lead promotes candidates. Skips tasks without a base sha; dedupes by source.
4. When the fingerprint of an arm's runs differs from the newest fingerprint for the same variant in that set, the report prints `baseline stale: <old> -> <new>` for that variant.
Release fragment line in docs/releases/unreleased/orchestrator-ab-variants.md.

The graded interface: a finished eval task carries `evalCheck: {code, tail}` in task.get.
tasks.check: git show 24a86d8:orchd/tests/eval_ab.rs > orchd/tests/zz_ref_check.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet --test zz_ref_check -- --exact a_done_eval_task_counts_as_a_success_only_when_its_check_passes 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 1 passed'

tasks.name: timeline-catalogue
tasks.request:
orchd task timeline and failure-signature catalogue, shown in the orchestrator panel

The owner cannot see where a task's time and money went, or which failures keep recurring across tasks. Add, repo-agnostically:
1. RPC `task.timeline {id}` -> ordered segments built from the task record and each run's events.jsonl: {stage (plan|implement|verify|review|advisor|final|wait), attempt, startedAt, endedAt, costUsd, outcome, failureKind?, buckets? (work_breakdown for implement attempts)}. Waiting for the owner is its own segment. Computed on demand, not stored.
2. RPC `failures.catalogue {repo?, sinceDays?}` -> failure signatures across tasks (the existing `failure.signature`), grouped: {signature, kind, count, tasks: [id,title], lastSeen, exampleDetail}, sorted by count. Also an `orchd failures` CLI printing the same as a table.
3. Panel (src/orchestrator/): the task detail gets a compact horizontal timeline bar (segments sized by duration, colored by stage with existing tokens, cost in the tooltip), and the orchestrator page gets a 'Recurring failures' list (top 10) that opens the example task. Follow the existing panel components and tokens; no new dependencies. Save screenshots of both with the ui-evidence recipe under artifacts/.
Mirror types in src/orchestrator/types.ts. Release fragment line.

The graded interface: `task.timeline {id}` returns `segments: [{stage, attempt, startedAt, endedAt, costUsd, outcome, failureKind?}]`; `failures.catalogue {}` returns rows `{signature, kind, count, tasks: [{id, title}], lastSeen, exampleDetail, exampleTaskId}`.
tasks.check: git show 9900979:orchd/tests/timeline.rs > orchd/tests/zz_ref_check.rs && cd orchd && cargo test --quiet --test zz_ref_check -- --exact task_timeline_orders_plan_implement_review_and_the_owner_wait_with_costs failures_catalogue_groups_two_tasks_with_one_signature_into_one_row 2>&1 | grep -q '^test result: ok. 2 passed'
